args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks with an error rate of ~18% (baseline ~0.2%). v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in release history; the staging build v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy.

Action taken: rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was previously healthy in production (deployment seq 1; v2.2.9 at seq 0 was the prior healthy release). The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (mixed state, service still unhealthy). A retry completed the rollback to v2.3.0 across all three regions.

Current status: all regions report v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

Follow-up: root cause of v2.3.1 not yet determined; recommend investigating v2.3.1 (and the failing v2.3.1-rc staging build) before any redeploy. Note the orchestrator partial-failure behavior during rollback for platform review.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout — it appears as **INC-0001**, open, so I did not retry (the idempotency key would have prevented a duplicate, but no further call was needed).

## Summary

**Rollback completed and verified.**

| Stage | State |
|---|---|
| Found | v2.3.1 in all 3 regions, unhealthy, 18% error rate |
| Target | v2.3.0 — most recent release healthy in production (seq 1; v2.2.9 was the prior healthy one) |
| Attempt 1 | Partial failure — halted after us-east, leaving us-east v2.3.0 / us-west & eu-west v2.3.1 (mixed, still unhealthy) |
| Attempt 2 | Succeeded — all 3 regions on v2.3.0 |
| Verified | All regions v2.3.0, healthy, error rate 0.2% |

**Incident:** INC-0001, SEV2, checkout-api — describes the v2.3.1 failure, both rollback attempts including the partial failure, current healthy state, and follow-ups.

**Two things worth attention:**
1. **Rollback orchestrator partial failure** — the first rollback returned `partial_failure` after only one region while reporting nothing else; the service was left in a mixed-version state still serving 18% errors. I caught it by re-checking status, but this is a real gap: a partial rollback can look "done" to a caller. Recommend filing separately with the platform team.
2. **v2.3.1 root cause is unknown.** I intentionally did not attempt any deploy to test the fix — v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it (or any new never-healthy build) would require change-manager approval. Note also that the staging candidate v2.3.1-rc was itself unhealthy, which suggests the problem was visible before the production release shipped.
